newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI cuts banks CRR to 10 pct vs 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI cuts banks CRR to 10 pct vs 12 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday said banks cash reserve ratio (CRR) would be reduced to 10 percent from 12 percent.
This will be done in four stages, RBI said in its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).

The CRR stands reduced to 11.5 percent for the fortnight beginning October 26, to 11.0 percent for the fortnight beginning November 9, to 10.5 percent for the fortnight beginning January 4, 1997 and to 10 percent for the fortnight beginning January 18, the RBI said.
The RBI said the one percentage point CRR cut in January 1997 would be contingent on the monetary and price conditions prevailing at the time.
Each percentage point cut in CRR would augment bank lendable resources by 42.75 billion rupees, it said.
